race_name: L'Etape Costa Rica by Tour de France

top_categories.workout_context: 102ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.

Road-specific control matters at L'Etape Costa Rica by Tour de France. Practice on volcanic paved climbs with Tour pedigree: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 80 miles.
Race-pace efforts that mimic L'Etape Costa Rica by Tour de France's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before August.
8,202ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
At L'Etape Costa Rica by Tour de France, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of L'Etape Costa Rica by Tour de France. Train it until it feels boring.
At mile 60 of 80, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
8,202ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 80 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.

Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at L'Etape Costa Rica by Tour de France. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
Low-cadence force work supports 8,202ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.
Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on volcanic paved climbs with Tour pedigree can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.

race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for L'Etape Costa Rica by Tour de France’s 80 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.altitude: L'Etape Costa Rica by Tour de France includes meaningful altitude exposure. Reduced oxygen availability can affect sustainable power, pacing, and recovery. Use a conservative upper-mountain pacing plan, test any travel or acclimatization strategy before the event, and plan layers for changing conditions. Do not begin iron or other supplements without clinician-guided testing. UV exposure at altitude.
